title: Rainfed cereal output swings with rainfall and collapsed in the 2023 drought, cutting the harvest by roughly two-thirds or more

rootCauses.cause: Over 85% of wheat area is rainfed (irrigated wheat under 15% of area; ITES: only 10% of cereal production is irrigated), so output depends on the amount and timing of winter and spring rain
Consecutive drought years (four by 2023) and heat during crop development; seed stocks depleted after failed harvests

excerpt: Tunisian cereals are mostly rainfed: irrigated wheat is under 15% of wheat area, and ITES says only 10% of cereal production comes from irrigated land. Output therefore moves with rainfall. Since 1990, cereal production…

sections.heading: Problem
sections.content: Tunisian cereals are mostly rainfed: irrigated wheat is under 15% of wheat area (SRC-TG-700), and ITES says only 10% of cereal production comes from irrigated land (SRC-TG-706). Output therefore moves with rainfall. Since 1990, cereal production has ranged from about 0.55 Mt (2002) to 2.9 Mt (1996) (SRC-TG-707). In 2023 a fourth consecutive dry year combined with heat at critical growth stages (SRC-TG-705, SRC-TG-700). Sources disagree on how far the harvest fell, and their scopes differ. FAO GIEWS first estimated 302,000 t, almost 80% below average. It later revised this to 520,000 t, about 70% below the five-year average (SRC-TG-700). The Ministry of Agriculture's figures reported by USDA give 442 kt wheat and 90 kt barley, about 532 kt (SRC-TG-704). World Bank WDI, using FAO data, gives 612 kt for all cereals (SRC-TG-707). The 2022 harvest had been about 1.69 Mt of wheat and barley (SRC-TG-704). Output recovered to about 1.5 Mt in 2024 and 1.7 Mt in 2025 (SRC-TG-700).

sections.heading: Root causes
sections.content:
A poor harvest is the symptom. Low yields are a co-symptom (see Evidence), not a cause. The underlying causes are these:

- **Exposure by design: a rainfed system.** Over 85% of wheat area relies on rain (SRC-TG-700), and only 10% of cereal production is irrigated (SRC-TG-706). FAO notes that this makes year-on-year output vary significantly (SRC-TG-700).
- **Climate shock, compounding over years.** 2023 was the fourth below-average rainfall year in a row (SRC-TG-705). FAO says the drought conditions had not been experienced in over two decades (SRC-TG-700). The failed 2022/23 durum harvest did not leave enough seed for 2023/24, so the government imported seed and farmers switched to barley (SRC-TG-700, SRC-TG-703). One bad year therefore weakens the next.
- **How failure shows in the data.** Yield per harvested hectare does not capture a collapse well. WDI yield for 2023 was 1,300 kg/ha, close to normal, because harvested area fell to 471,000 ha (SRC-TG-707). USDA's Ministry-based tables show 952,000 ha of wheat and barley seeded but only 437,000 ha harvested in MY 2023/24 (SRC-TG-704). The earlier USDA report had 634,000 ha harvested (SRC-TG-703). Much of the sown area was simply not harvested.

**What the evidence does not support.** We found no clear evidence that average yields are falling. Our calculation from WDI gives a mean of 1,246 kg/ha over 1990-1999 and 1,473 kg/ha over 2015-2024 (SRC-TG-707). Variability is similar or slightly higher: the coefficient of variation is 16.8% in the 1990s and 19.1% over 2015-2024 (SRC-TG-707). ITES describes a "slight downward trend" in cereal production, in a section whose chart covers 2004-2018 (SRC-TG-706). The problem is better stated as low and highly volatile yields than as declining yields.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.content:
- Office des Céréales collection (SRC-TG-705). In 2023 it collected 286.7 kt durum, 6.2 kt soft wheat and 0.5 kt barley, 293.4 kt in total. This compares with 756.4 kt on average in 2020-2022 and 1,284.7 kt in 2019. GIEWS gives government purchases of 225.6 kt in 2023 against 700 kt in 2022 (SRC-TG-700). The two sources disagree on the 2023 figure.
- Consequence for imports and finance: in 2023/24 monthly import needs rose to about 100,000 t for durum and 100,000 t for barley. The Office des Céréales faced an extra financing gap of about US$522 million (SRC-TG-705).
- Yield level (co-symptom): over 2010-2018, yields did not exceed 25 q/ha for durum, 21 q/ha for soft wheat and 16 q/ha for barley, averaging 18 q/ha (SRC-TG-706). A signed analysis article in the ONAGRI Lettre ranks Tunisia 120th of 191 countries for cereal yields. It links low yields to climate, land quality, inputs and practices, without quantifying each factor (SRC-TG-701, secondary analysis, tier B weight).
- Recovery depends on rain: GIEWS attributes the 2025 harvest (about 1.7 Mt, 18% above average) to April-May rainfall (SRC-TG-700). USDA states that wheat yields depend on April rainfall, which can improve them by 10-20% when favourable (SRC-TG-704).
- Future (context only, no projection block). One modelling study (AquaCrop, Med-CORDEX) reports, against its baseline, temperature up 4 °C and precipitation down 37% by the end of the century; the abstract does not name the scenario for these two figures. It gives a durum yield gap of 45-55% under RCP 8.5, and says that under RCP 8.5 the north-west would become unsuited to rainfed wheat (SRC-TG-708). A second study at two north-west sites for 2041-2070 does not report a clear decline and stresses model sensitivity (SRC-TG-709). Only abstracts were read. These do not support a sourced national projection, so no predicted finding is made.

sections.heading: Why confidence is what it is
sections.content: High that cereal output is rainfall-driven and that 2023 was a severe failure: GIEWS, USDA/Ministry, the World Bank (OC data) and WDI all agree. Medium overall because the size of the 2023 shortfall differs across sources (302-612 kt), harvested-area figures were revised, and the Ministry's own publication was not opened directly. The long-term yield trend and future projections are weak or contested.

sections.heading: Links to other sectors
sections.content:
- Water: the dependence on rainfall is the water side of this problem. Irrigation is being promoted to stabilise wheat, with an irrigation water subsidy of USD 0.07/m3 and a target of 120,000 ha of irrigated wheat (SRC-TG-704). Expanding irrigated wheat would therefore add to irrigation water demand; the size of that demand was not sourced (see data_gaps).
- Livestock: barley collection fell to almost nothing in 2023 (SRC-TG-705), and barley is consumed mainly in feedlots and as supplemental feed (SRC-TG-704). This links to the `livestock-feed` theme.

sections.heading: Leads for phase 2
sections.content:
- FIDAC (Fonds d'indemnisation des dommages agricoles causés par les calamités naturelles), strengthened in the 2024 Finance Law (SRC-TG-705)
- Seasonal credit for grain producers (2024 Finance Law) (SRC-TG-705)
- Certified seed subsidy and seed multiplication after the 2023 seed shortage (SRC-TG-703)
- Delayed sowing dates as a climate adaptation strategy (SRC-TG-708)
- Conservation agriculture or no-till on durum wheat (seen in search results, not opened)
- Drought-tolerant varieties from INRAT and INGC (ONAGRI Lettre 2022 variety list, SRC-TG-701)
- Supplementary irrigation of wheat towards 120,000 ha (SRC-TG-704)

sections.heading: Verification
sections.content: **Independent review, 21 November 2026:** pass after corrections. Checked against the originals: GIEWS country briefs of 29 November 2023 (p.14) and 30 May 2024 (p.12) (SRC-TG-700); USDA GAIN TS2026-0004 Tables 1-2 and TS2024-0003 Table 1 (SRC-TG-704, SRC-TG-703); World Bank PAD5602 Table 1 and paragraph 9 (SRC-TG-705); World Bank WDI AG.PRD.CREL.MT 2023 and the yield series rows 1990-2024, with the 1990-2024 production range (0.55 Mt in 2002, 2.9 Mt in 1996) rechecked on the API (SRC-TG-707); ITES section "La production de cereales" (SRC-TG-706). Corrections: the ITES "slight downward trend" is no longer tied to 2010-2018 (its chart covers 2004-2018); the WDI production citation gap is recorded in data_gaps. Independent teammate sign-off is outstanding; reviewer and author share the TahaGHZ identity, so the record is not validated.

resolvedSources.title: GIEWS Country Brief: The Republic of Tunisia (archive of briefs 2010-2026)
resolvedSources.publisher: FAO Global Information and Early Warning System (GIEWS)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Brief of 29 November 2023 (archive PDF, brief dated 29-November-2023):

> Cereal cultivation is mostly rainfed, resulting in significant year-on-year variations. The irrigated wheat area represents less than 15 percent of the total wheat planted area.

> Coupled with above-average temperatures during the critical crop development stages, severe drought conditions, not experienced in the country for over two decades, constrained crop development, leading to widespread crop failures. Consequently, 2023 cereal output was estimated at 302 000 tonnes, almost 80 percent below the average.

> In 2023, the guaranteed farmgate prices of durum wheat increased to TDD 1 300 (USD 436), up from TDD 1 000/tonne (USD 339). The guaranteed farmgate prices of soft (common) wheat increased from TDD 800 (USD 271) to TDD 1 000/tonne (USD 336) and those of barley from TDD 690 (USD 233) to TDD 800 (USD 267). In 2023, the government purchased 225 600 tonnes of grains, compared to 700 000 tonnes in 2022.

> Cereal import requirements in the 2023/24 marketing year (July/June) are forecast at 4.7 million tonnes, about 30 percent above the average import requirements of the previous year. More than half of the imported cereals is wheat.

> Between 2016 and 2020, the country sourced almost 40 percent of its wheat imports from Ukraine, 7 percent from the Russian Federation and the rest from various European Union countries.

> In spite of the country's high import dependency rate, changes in international prices of wheat products and vegetable oil are not fully transmitted into domestic prices as the government's universal food subsidy programme keeps them stable. There have been discussions about reforming the subsidy system, which puts a significant burden on the national budget, but the implementation has been postponed so far.

Brief of 30 May 2024:

> The aggregate 2023 cereal output, mainly wheat, is estimated at 520 000 tonnes, about 70 percent below the five-year average.

> The country relies heavily on grain imports, even in years with good domestic production, and cereals constitute the largest share of the value of imports.

> Imports cover more than half of the country's cereal consumption needs. Cereal imports in the 2023/24 marketing year (July/June) are forecast at 4 million tonnes and above the five-year average.

> Durum wheat for couscous and pasta, and soft wheat for bread, represent the main components of the local diet and account for around 45 percent of the food calorie intake.

> Four consecutive years of drought have weakened the seed production system and the 2022/23 harvest of durum wheat was not sufficient to guarantee seeds for the 2023/24 campaign. As a consequence, the government increased imports of wheat seed, while some farmers decided to shift to barley production.

> In the period between July 2023 and May 2024, the Russian Federation and Ukraine supplied about half of the wheat imports to the country, while about 30 percent was supplied by Bulgaria and Turkey.

> the rise of international food prices translated into increased value of subsidies leading to public debt growth and reduced the country's import capacity, causing shortages of basic food products such as wheat, coffee, tea and vegetable oils.

Brief of 27 July 2022:

> The country aims to reach an annual domestic production of 3 million tonnes of cereals to achieve self-sufficiency.

> In 2022, the average import prices of durum wheat so far reached USD 665/tonne, up from USD 435 in 2021 and USD 327 in 2020. Likewise, import prices paid for 1 tonne of soft (common) wheat increased from USD 231 in 2020 to USD 307 in 2021 and USD 416 in 2022.

Brief of 26 March 2025:

> Cereal production in 2024 is estimated at about 1.5 million tonnes, nearly three times higher than the drought-affected 2023 output, yet remaining about 6 percent below the five-year average.

Brief of 18 February 2026:

> Cereal production in 2025 is estimated at about 1.7 million tonnes, nearly 18 percent above the five-year average, reflecting improved weather conditions during the second half of the season. Although the season started with dry weather conditions between October 2024 and February 2025, above-average rainfall amounts between April and May boosted yields in key producing regions.

> Although local production has increased over the past two years, it covers about 60 percent of domestic annual needs and the country continues to rely on international markets to secure an adequate supply of wheat for local consumption.
resolvedSources.notes: The archive PDF was downloaded and converted with pdftotext; the extracts above are prose paragraphs, not tables. GIEWS revised its 2023 estimate from 302 000 t (Nov 2023) to 520 000 t (May 2024); both values are kept. GIEWS figures are FAO estimates built on its Country Cereal Balance Sheet, not Tunisian official statistics. Marketing year is July/June.

resolvedSources.publisher: Observatoire National de l'Agriculture (ONAGRI), Ministère de l'Agriculture
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article "bilan apport-utilisation", p. 9 (blé dur), sources INS-OC-DGPA:

> La dépendance de la consommation aux importations a été de 35% en 2021

English gloss: the dependence of (durum wheat) consumption on imports was 35% in 2021.

p. 10 (blé tendre):

> Entre 2020 et 2021 la production utilisable a passé de 75,7 mille tonnes à 104,7 mille tonnes. Ce qui n'a pas empêché une progression des importations entre les deux dernières années et sur la période d'étude puisqu'elles ont augmenté avec un taux annuel moyen de 1,1%

> La consommation tunisienne en blé tendre a été de 1221,7 mille tonnes en 2021.

> Durant 2021, le coefficient de dépendance étrangère du blé tendre était de 93,1.

> Par habitant, la consommation était de 101,6 kg/habitant en 2021. Cette consommation est supérieure à celle estimée par l'enquête sur la consommation des ménages effectuée par l'INS, qui était de l'ordre de 84,9kg per capita en 2015 contre 72 kg par personne en 1990.

English gloss (last sentence): per capita soft wheat consumption was 101.6 kg in 2021, above the 84.9 kg per capita estimated by the INS household consumption survey in 2015 (72 kg in 1990).

English gloss: usable soft wheat production rose from 75.7 kt (2020) to 104.7 kt (2021), yet imports kept growing (1.1% a year over 2018-2021). Soft wheat consumption was 1,221.7 kt in 2021. In 2021 the foreign dependence coefficient of soft wheat was 93.1 (%).

p. 11 (orge):

> Durant 2021, le coefficient de dépendance étrangère de l'orge était de 75,6%.

English gloss: in 2021 the foreign dependence coefficient of barley was 75.6%.

p. 12 (conclusion):

> On a pu déceler, essentiellement pour le blé dur et l'orge, une variation du coefficient de dépendance étrangère d'une année à l'autre selon les conditions climatiques.

English gloss: for durum wheat and barley especially, the foreign dependence coefficient varies from year to year with climatic conditions.

Article on the cereal sector, p. 25:

> la production des céréales est marquée par une grande irrégularité, les progrès techniques réalisés au niveau du secteur agricole ne sont pas parvenus à stabiliser le secteur. La Tunisie est classée 120 mondialement sur un total de 191 pays en matière de rendement des cultures céréalières.

> Le faible rendement des céréales est lié aux conditions climatiques, à la qualité des terres, aux intrants et aux pratiques agricoles.

> Les céréales contribuent avec 49,2% aux apports caloriques de la ration

English gloss: cereal output is very irregular; technical progress has not stabilised the sector. Tunisia ranks 120th of 191 countries for cereal yields. Low cereal yields are linked to climatic conditions, land quality, inputs and farming practices. Cereals provide 49.2% of dietary calories.

p. 26:

> La Tunisie n'est pas autosuffisante en produits céréalier et importe presque 50% de ses besoins, un taux susceptible d'atteindre 75% dans les prochaines années avec la détérioration des conditions climatiques (Tanchum, 2021)

English gloss: Tunisia imports almost 50% of its cereal needs, a rate that could reach 75% in coming years as climate conditions worsen (citing Tanchum, 2021).
resolvedSources.notes: ONAGRI is the Ministry of Agriculture's observatory; the balance-sheet article uses INS, Office des Céréales and DGPA data and assumes usable production is 90% of production. The tables (Tableaux 1-3) extracted with shifted columns, so only prose sentences are quoted. The "75%" projection is secondary (cites Tanchum 2021, not opened) and has no stated method. The articles in the same issue are signed by individual authors. Only the balance-sheet article (pp. 9-12, INS/OC/DGPA data) carries tier A weight. The cereal-sector article on pp. 25-26 is a signed secondary analysis and should be weighted as tier B: its yield ranking (120 of 191) is unsourced there, and the "almost 50%" and "75%" figures come from other authors.

Production policy:

> To achieve the government's self-sufficiency goal of reaching average annual production of 3 MMT for cereals, of which 1.7 MMT is durum wheat, state-sponsored programs include:

> The Grain Board (OC) is an SOE created in 1962 under the tutelage of Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries (MAWRF) with a core mandate to regulate and ensure a stable supply of grain on the domestic market through domestic grain harvest collection, imports, and the management of strategic reserves.

resolvedSources.title: La sécurité alimentaire de la Tunisie à l'horizon 2035
resolvedSources.publisher: Institut Tunisien des Études Stratégiques (ITES), hosted by ONAGRI
resolvedSources.extracts:
Page numbers are PDF page numbers (printed numbers differ). Study dated December 2023, addressed to the President of the Republic.

PDF p. 27 (policy review 1960-1970):

> Pour le développement de la production de céréales, un Office des Céréales (OC) a été créé en 1962

English gloss: to develop cereal production, an Office des Céréales was created in 1962.

PDF p. 32 (price policy periods, after Khaldi and Naili 1995):

> Le blocage des prix et des salaires (1960-1970) : au cours de cette période, la politique de l'Etat en matière de prix à la production consistait en la fixation et le maintien des prix des produits agricoles à un niveau bas.

> La mise en place des subventions (1970-1984) : en 1971, la Caisse Générale de Compensation (CGC) est créée pour gérer un système de

English gloss: 1960-1970, the state fixed producer prices of agricultural products at a low level; 1970-1984, subsidies set up — in 1971 the CGC was created to manage a subsidy system.

PDF p. 33:

> Les seuls produits qui continuent après à être subventionnés sont les céréales d'alimentation humaine, l'huile

English gloss: after structural adjustment, the only products still subsidised are cereals for human consumption, (vegetable) oil [and others].

PDF p. 33 (citing INS 2013, analysis of the impact of food subsidies on poverty):

> qu'en 2010, seules 9,2 % des subventions sont orientées aux ménages les plus démunis, 60,5 % aux ménages de la classe moyenne, 7,5 % à la population aisée, alors que 22,8 % sont transférés hors ménages, notamment vers les entreprises de restauration hors foyer.

English gloss: in 2010 only 9.2% of subsidies went to the poorest households, 60.5% to middle-class households, 7.5% to the well-off, and 22.8% outside households, notably to out-of-home catering businesses.

PDF p. 52 (stability of access):

> Selon l'INC, le gaspillage du pain par les ménages a atteint les 900.000 pains/j, ce qui correspond à une valeur moyenne de l'ordre de 100 millions DT/an.

English gloss: according to the INC, household bread waste reached 900,000 loaves a day, worth about 100 million TND a year (no year given).

PDF p. 53:

> Le taux de dépendance vis-à-vis des céréales importées reste en moyenne de l'ordre de 60%, soit : • 40% pour le blé dur ; • 80% pour le blé tendre ; • 50% pour l'orge

English gloss: dependence on imported cereals averages about 60%: 40% durum wheat, 80% soft wheat, 50% barley.

PDF p. 54:

> La production céréalière connait une légère tendance à la baisse, malgré les investissements et les soutiens de l'Etat. [...] Elle est en grande partie issue des cultures pluviales (seulement 10% en irrigué) et reste soumise aux aléas climatiques.

> La moyenne se situe autour de 17 millions de Tonnes durant la période 2010-2018. Les rendements n'excèdent pas les 25 q/ha pour le blé dur, 21 q/ha pour le blé tendre et 16 q/ha pour l'orge avec une moyenne de 18q/ha pour la même période.

> La production de blé dur prédomine et progresse vu son adaptation aux conditions locales (+27% entre 2010-2018), contre un recul du blé tendre (-25%).

English gloss: cereal production shows a slight downward trend despite state investment and support; it is mostly rainfed (only 10% irrigated) and exposed to climate hazards. Average around "17 million tonnes" (sic) over 2010-2018. Yields do not exceed 25 q/ha durum, 21 q/ha soft wheat, 16 q/ha barley, average 18 q/ha. Durum production up 27% over 2010-2018, soft wheat down 25%.

PDF p. 55:

> La part de l'office des céréales dans la collecte physique a fortement diminué passant de 32% en 2005 à 2% en 2012, au profit d'opérateurs privés désormais majoritaires (58%) et des sociétés mutuelles de service agricoles (SMSA) (40%).

English gloss: OC's share of physical collection fell from 32% in 2005 to 2% in 2012, in favour of private operators (58%) and agricultural service cooperatives (40%).

PDF p. 116 (printed p. 114; page corrected by source-verifier, previously given as p. 121), trend micro-scenario (H1, "au fil de l'eau"), horizon 2035, V12-H1:

> La dépendance au marché international se poursuit pour les produits de base et les intrants (Taux de dépendance moyen des céréales 57% dont le Blé tendre avec 84%, le blé dur 41% et l'orge 51%)

PDF p. 108, footnote 94 to the same figures: (footnote text not found again by text search on re-check; page unconfirmed)

> Maintien de la moyenne des dix dernières années. Source : Observatoire Tunisien de l'Economie, 2023. Dépendance aux importations de blé.

English gloss: in the trend scenario to 2035, average cereal dependence stays at 57% (soft wheat 84%, durum 41%, barley 51%); the footnote says this is the ten-year average held constant (source Observatoire Tunisien de l'Economie, 2023).

### Livestock feed extracts (added for FND-TG-760/761)

PDF p. 55:

> sachant que la demande augmentera de 50% pour les céréales et doublera pour les aliments de bétail (SOLIDAR et PAM, 2020)

English gloss: by 2035 demand will rise 50% for cereals and double for livestock feed (citing SOLIDAR and WFP, 2020).

PDF p. 66 (section II.2.1.1 Disponibilité, Covid-19 and 2021-2022 shocks):

> les aliments de bétail, qui sont en grande partie importés (30% des besoins en graines de maïs, de blé fourrager, de tourteau de Soja et d'orge). La valeur des importations en 2021 a enregistré un accroissement significatif par rapport à 2019 (Fig. 1), soit 75% contre 26%. Ceci résulte essentiellement de l'accroissement des quantités importées, (surtout du tourteau de soja de 85% et de l'orge de 64%), mais aussi de la volatilité de leur prix sur le marché mondial (Fig. 2) et de la dévaluation du dinar tunisien. Les augmentations des prix ont atteint en 2021 un accroissement de 48% pour le maïs, 30% pour l'orge et 18% pour le soja.

English gloss: livestock feed is largely imported ("30% of needs" for maize, feed wheat, soybean meal and barley, as printed). The value of feed imports in 2021 rose 75% over 2019, mainly because of higher import volumes (soybean meal +85%, barley +64%), but also world price volatility and the devaluation of the Tunisian dinar. Prices rose in 2021 by 48% for maize, 30% for barley and 18% for soya.

> Vu l'augmentation drastique du cours de la matière première, les prix du concentré ont enregistré une hausse de 35% en 2022 par rapport à 2019. Il est prévu que la tendance haussière des prix du concentré va se poursuivre à un rythme plus rapide, ce qui constituera une menace sérieuse pour le secteur de l'élevage.

English gloss: concentrate feed prices rose 35% in 2022 compared with 2019; the upward trend is expected to continue faster, a serious threat to livestock farming.

> D'autres ont abandonné partiellement ou totalement leurs activités (tel le cas pour l'élevage avicole et laitier).

English gloss: some farmers partly or fully abandoned their activity (as in poultry and dairy farming).

PDF p. 66, Covid-19 and 2021-2022 shocks (continuation):

> D'autres ont abandonné partiellement ou totalement leurs activités (tel le cas pour l'élevage avicole et laitier).

English gloss: some poultry and dairy farmers partly or fully abandoned their activity in the context of the Covid-19 and input-price shocks; the study cites the IACE/UTAP 2021 survey.

PDF pp. 69-70 (2022 supply disruption):

> Concrètement, les chiffres montrent que c'est surtout l'orge qui a subi de fortes baisses à l'importation d'où l'explication, en partie, de l'indisponibilité temporaire de quantités suffisantes d'aliments de bétail qui a agi sur la disponibilité du lait et autres sources alimentaires de protéines animales.

> Au niveau du citoyen, ceci s'est ressenti sous forme de légères pénuries durant quelques semaines.

> L'opportunisme des intermédiaires et la spéculation de certains commerçants semblent avoir accentué cette crise temporaire.

English gloss: barley imports fell sharply (2022), partly explaining a temporary feed shortage affecting milk and other animal protein availability; consumers felt light shortages for a few weeks. Intermediary opportunism and some traders’ speculation appear to have worsened the crisis.
resolvedSources.notes: ITES is a state think tank attached to the Presidency; tier B. The 2010-2018 production sentence mixes units ("17 millions de Tonnes" is almost certainly quintals, i.e. about 1.7 Mt; elsewhere "26 MT" for 2009); it is quoted but not used as an indicator. The 2035 "projection" is a scenario assumption (ten-year average held constant), not a model. The CGC creation year here (1971) differs from the World Bank (1970, SRC-TG-705).

resolvedSources.title: World Development Indicators: cereal yield (AG.YLD.CREL.KG), cereal production (AG.PRD.CREL.MT), land under cereal production (AG.LND.CREL.HA), Tunisia 1990-2024
resolvedSources.notes: The underlying data are FAOSTAT (FAOSTAT itself was unreachable on 2026-11-21, HTTP 521). The 2023 production figure (all cereals) is higher than the GIEWS and USDA estimates (see SRC-TG-700, SRC-TG-703); the mean and CV are our own computation.

resolvedSources.title: Projected long-term climate change impacts on rainfed durum wheat production and sustainable adaptation strategies
resolvedSources.publisher: Journal of Cleaner Production, vol. 494, 144980 (Ghazouani H., Jabnoun R., Harzallah A., Ibrahimi K., Amami R., Boughattas I., Milham P., Ghfar A.A., Provenzano G., Sher F.)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Abstract (retrieved via OpenAlex API record for the DOI and the Western Sydney University repository page):

> a field and modelling study was conducted using the AquaCrop model and a set of simulated climate data from the Med-CORDEX initiative to analyse the effects of climate change on the environment, production, and water productivity (WP) of wheat under two representative concentration pathways (RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5) during 2040–2050 and 2080–2090

> Results showed that in comparison with the base line period ( BL ) the average temperature increased by +4 °C, precipitation decreased −37%, crop cycle duration declined by ∼5 d/decade, reference evapotranspiration diminished to reach 511 mm, irrigation requirements rose to 736 mm, years requiring irrigation increasing from 3 ( BL) to 9 and yield gap augmented to reach 55% by the end of the 21st century.

> Despite delaying the sowing date, the harvest losses remain important (yield gap of 45–55% under the RCP 8.5 scenario), requiring further adaptation strategies.

Highlight:

> For RCP 8.5, the north-west of Tunisia will be unsuited to rainfed wheat.
resolvedSources.notes: Only the abstract was read; the full text (paywalled) was not opened, so the baseline period, site and the exact 2040-2050 figures are not known. The +4 °C and -37% values are end-of-century under RCP 8.5. "Yield gap" may be measured against potential (irrigated) yield rather than current yield. Single crop model and single regional climate model.

resolvedSources.title: Future Impact of Climate Change on Durum Wheat Growth and Productivity in Northern Tunisia
resolvedSources.publisher: Agronomy 14(9), 2022, MDPI (El Melki M.N., Souissi I., Al-Khayri J.M., Al-Dossary O., Alsubaie B., Khlifi S.)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Abstract (retrieved via OpenAlex API record for the DOI):

> This study evaluates the projected impact of climate change on wheat production in Northwest Tunisia, specifically at Medjez El Beb (36.67 m, 9.74°) and Slougia (36.66 m, 9.6°), for the period 2041–2070. Using the CNRM-CM5.1 and GFDL-ESM2M climate models under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 scenarios, coupled with the AquaCrop and SIMPLE crop growth models

> Under RCP4.5, projected average yields are 7.709 q/ha with AquaCrop and 7.703 q/ha with GFDL-ESM2M. Under RCP8.5, yields are 7.765 tons/ha with AquaCrop and 7.198 q/ha with SIMPLE Crop, indicating that reduced emissions could improve wheat growth conditions.

> These findings emphasize the importance of model selection and calibration for accurately projecting the agricultural impacts of climate change
resolvedSources.notes: Only the abstract was read (mdpi.com returned HTTP 403). The abstract mixes units (q/ha and tons/ha for similar numbers) and does not state a change against a baseline, so no percentage change can be derived. Two sites only. Cited here to show that projections for Tunisian wheat are not consistent across studies.

The state cereal system (Office des Céréales monopoly, decreed prices, CGC subsidies) built in 1962-1971 now strains public finances and blunts market signals
